messages:
maria: Anyone else seeing DNS failures for internal services after the node-pool rollout this morning? healthchecks spiking 502s on a few clusters.

sam: Yup, noticed intermittent inability to resolve svc names from app pods. Started ~09:12 UTC right after the pool rotated.

maria: Example: dig against cluster DNS sometimes returns nothing.
```
$ kubectl exec -n foo svc-a-123 -- dig @10.96.0.10 svc-a.foo.svc.cluster.local +short
# sometimes empty, sometimes returns IP
```

alex: coredns pods are hitting CPU/latency spikes and logs show repeated forward errors. log excerpt: 
```
[INFO] 2026-03-18T09:13:01Z forward: error: lookup svc-a.foo.svc.cluster.local on 127.0.0.1:53: read udp 127.0.0.1:53123->127.0.0.1:53: i/o timeout
[WARN] 2026-03-18T09:13:02Z plugin/forward: failed to forward: context deadline exceeded
```

dani: I pulled the Corefile and node resolv.conf on a repro node. Corefile forwards to the host resolver (127.0.0.1) as upstream. Host /etc/resolv.conf got rewritten and now points to the cluster DNS 10.96.0.10. That creates a circular forwarding path (coredns -> host resolver -> cluster DNS).

ops-oncall: Repro steps I ran quickly: 
```
# on host node after rollout
$ cat /etc/resolv.conf
nameserver 10.96.0.10
# coredns Corefile snippet
forward . 127.0.0.1
```
So coredns is forwarding queries to 127.0.0.1 on the node, and the node ends up pointing back to the cluster DNS IP. Loop.

infra-bot: deployment "node-agent" rolled 2026-03-18T09:05:23Z to ami-20260315 -> changed host dns config fallback behavior (see deploy link).

sam: For a quick mitigation I'm going to change the CoreDNS upstreams to public resolvers and roll coredns. That should break the cycle and restore name resolution while we investigate host agent behavior.

maria: Agreed. Note external name lookups may be impacted briefly. Use this patch: 
```
kubectl -n kube-system patch configmap coredns --patch '{"data":{"Corefile":".:53 {\n    errors\n    health\n    ready\n    kubernetes cluster.local in-addr.arpa ip6.arpa {\n      pods insecure\n      fallthrough in-addr.arpa ip6.arpa\n    }\n    prometheus :9153\n    forward . 8.8.8.8 1.1.1.1\n    cache 30\n    loop\n    reload\n}\n"}}' --type=merge
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment coredns
```

alex: Patch applied and restarted. Observing coredns CPU trending down, internal svc resolution stabilized within a minute.

maria: Good catch. Root cause looks like host DNS agent changed behavior during the node image update and started preferring the cluster DNS IP, which we accidentally used as a host upstream in Corefile. That circular chain causes intermittent timeouts and heavy retrying.

dani: I'll open an infra ticket to revert the agent change and add a guard: CoreDNS config must not list any cluster IP from kube-system as an upstream. Adding a CI check to our config testing to detect 'forward to cluster service IP' will help prevent this.

ops-oncall: Filed INFRA-9822 with steps + rollback plan and a short postmortem template. Also add a note to the runbook to check /etc/resolv.conf on hosts after OS/image updates.

maria: Thanks all. Follow-up items: (1) revert node-agent behavior in a controlled rollout, (2) add admission/CI check for Corefile upstreams, (3) postmortem and RCA. Marking this resolved for now since service resolution is back. :thumbsup:
